headline: Approved $1,880,117 for Fitchburg Public Library renovation and report declaring Westminster Street land surplus for sale
summary: Council also gave final approval to a parking ban on the north side of Birch Street Passway and to three ordinance changes to Chapter 169 of the city code. It sent zoning moratorium petitions on battery storage and large data centers to the Planning Board, and referred two Unitil pole requests to an October 20, 2026 public hearing.
decisions: Accepted Appointments Committee report, 10-0.
Referred mayor's appointment letters to the Appointments Committee.
Approved September 15, 2026 council minutes as amended, 11-0.
Filed promotion of Captain Ryan Cringan to Permanent Deputy Chief.
Approved City Property Committee report, including sale by RFP of 465 and 0 Westminster St and Laurel Hill Cemetery Parcel A, 11-0.
Adopted $1,880,117 from available funds, as amended, for Fitchburg Public Library renovation, 11-0.
Adopted $42,384 appropriation charged to Reserve for Other Municipal Purposes for police, parking, and benefit accounts, 11-0.
Adopted $4,716 appropriation charged to Airport Receipts Reserved for personal services, 11-0.
Referred zoning moratorium petitions on battery storage systems and large data centers to the Planning Board for a public hearing, 11-0.
Held petition for temporary repairs to a private way on Greenhurst Ave.
Granted request to install a berm at 508 Milk Street.
Granted request to install a berm at 77 Congress St, as amended.
Referred $20,000 STEAM grant expenditure and $15,000 Coggshall Park donation orders to Finance.
Adopted order authorizing the City Clerk to notify voters of the November 3, 2026 State Election, 11-0.
Sent ordinance amending City Code §3-19 and §3-43 on City Clerk duties to first and second reading, 11-0.
Sent ordinance to repeal General Ordinance Chapter 164 in its entirety to first and second reading, 11-0.
Passed final reading of ordinance amending Chapter 169, § 59, 11-0.
Passed final reading of ordinance amending Chapter 169, § 76, 11-0.
Passed final reading of ordinance amending Chapter 169, § 77, 11-0.
Passed final reading of ordinance prohibiting parking on the north side of Birch Street Passway, 11-0.
Referred special legislation on creditable service of Marisa R. Fleming to Legislative Affairs.
Referred Unitil petition to relocate Pole #8 at 7 Beekman St to public hearing on October 20, 2026.
Referred Unitil petition for new midspan Pole #30A at 470 Alpine Road to public hearing on October 20, 2026.
Referred request for parking controls along Broad and Circle streets near Crocker Field to the Public Safety Committee.

City of Fitchburg  
                             Massachusetts 01420  
 
                     CITY COUNCIL  
            
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Fitchburg was held at the Legislative Building 
at 700 Main Street and over the Zoom meeting platform and live streamed at FATV Studios, 
Fitchburg, on October 6, 2026.   
 
The meeting was called to orde r by President Zarrella at 7:01 P.M.  The meeting opened with a 
salute to the Flag led by Councilor Cruz. The City Clerk called the roll 10 Councilors were present, 
(Councilo Cragin absent). Board consists of 11 members.  
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
I. PUBLIC FORUM 
  
No one spoke during Public Forum. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
II. ANNOUNCEMENTS 
The next meeting of the Widowed Helping Widowed Support Group will take place on Thursday, 
October 15 from 4 until 5:30 p.m. in Room 205 at the Fitchburg State University Recreation 
Center, 130 North Street. Kelley Lynn, Kathy Boisvert, and Bernie Schultz will co-facilitate the 
meeting. 
---- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------  
 
III. REPORT OF THE APPOINTMENTS COMMITTEE 
 
Appointments Committee 
Oral Report 
Meeting of October 6, 2026 
 
New Appointment letters: 
Full Time Student Police Officers 
For the City of Fitchburg 
Zackary Legros 
Benjamin Graciani 
Karina Rosado 
Anthony Stowell 
Sarah St. Peter 
 
Councilors at Large 
    Sally H. Cragin 
Amy L. Green 
Kevin T. Starr  
Elizabeth R. Walsh 
Anthony M. Zarrella 
 
President 
Anthony M. Zarrella 
 
Vice President 
Derrick J. Cruz 
         Ward Councilors 
   Ward 1 – Bernard J. Schultz III 
   Ward 2 – Paul R. Beauchemin 
   Ward 3 – Joseph S. Bowen, Jr. 
   Ward 4 – Andrew J. Van Hazinga 
   Ward 5 – Marisa R. Fleming 
   Ward 6 – Derrick J. Cruz
Report read and accepted by unanimous consent 10/0. 10 members present. Board consists of 11 
members. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
Councilor Cragin joined at 7:11 PM 
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
IV. REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON RECORDS 
 
• Joint Convention of the City Council and the School Committee meeting minutes of 
September 14, 2026 
• Regular City Council meeting minutes of September 15, 2026 
 
Motion and second to amend the minutes of the Regular City Council meeting of September 15, 
2026 by unanimous consent 11/0. 
 
Motion and second to approve the minutes as amended by unanimous consent 11/0. 11 members 
present. Board consist of 11 members. 
 
Report read and accepted minutes were adopted by unanimous consent 11/0. 11 members present. 
Board consists of 11 members. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
V. COMMUNICATION 
Her Honor the Mayor 
 
1. New-Appointment letter: 
    Miatta Edo-Osagie, as a Member of the Fitchburg Agricultural Commission, for a term to expire  
    on October 1, 2029. 
 
2. New-Appointment letters: 
    Fitchburg Cultural Council 
    Abigail Battles, for a term to expire on October 1, 2029. 
    Racheal Xavier, for a term to expire on October 1, 2029. 
    Stephanie Lee, for a term to expire on October 1, 2029. 
 
3. Re-Appointment letter: 
    Dominic Iacopino, as a Member of the Fitchburg Agricultural Commission, for a term to expire  
    on April 1, 2028. 
 
4. Re-Appointment letter: 
    James K. Momanyi, as a Member of the Fitchburg Agricultural Commission, for a term to  
    Expire on April 1, 2028. 
 
Appointments stand referred to the Appointments Committee.  
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Promotion Letter 
 
1. Promotion letter: 
            Captain Ryan Cringan to Permanent Deputy Chief. 
 
 
Promotion read and filed in the City Clerk’s Office.  
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
VI. REPORT OF COMMITTEES 
 
City Property Committee   
Meeting of October 6, 2026 
Oral Report 
 
156-26. Liz Murphy, Executive Director of Community Development & Planning, City of 
Fitchburg, is requesting that City Council declare surplus and authorize the sale of 
the following properties through an RFP Process: 
 
• 465 Westminster St 
Assessor’s Map W-2-A 
• 0 Westminster St 
Assessor’s Map W-2-1A 
 
157-26. Paula Caron, Chair, Fitchburg Planning Board, Petition to designate Ross Street 
between North Street and Blossom Street, and the entirety of Flat Rock Road, as 
Scenic Roads. 
 
158-26. Paula Caron, Chair, Fitchburg Planning Board Liz Murphy, Executive Director of 
Community Development, as outlined in the attached letter and plan of land, 
request to declare the surveyed portion of Laurel Hill Cemetery, identified as Parcel 
A, surplus to the City’s needs and make the property available for sale and 
development through an RFP process. 
 
Motion and second to approve the report of the City Property Committee by unanimous consent  
11/0. 11 members present. Board consists of 11 members. 
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Finance Committee 
Meeting of September 23, 2026 
Oral Report 
 
152-26. ORDER THAT: there be and hereby is appropriated the sum of FORTY-TWO 
THOUSAND THREE HUNDRED EIGHTY-FOUR DOLLARS ($42,384) same to 
be charged against RESERVE FOR OTHER MUNICIPAL PURPOSES and 
credited to the following Personal Services accounts: 
 
TREASURER – Parking Officer     $1,352 
POLICE – Dispatch  Salary    $33,393 
POLICE – Dispatch Overtime     $4,010 
POLICE – Holiday        $2,171 
POLICE – Clothing        $1,000 
EMPLOYEE BENEFITS – Buybacks        $458 
(Be Adopted) 
 
153-26. ORDER THAT: there be and hereby is appropriated the sum of FOUR 
THOUSAND SEVEN HUNDRED SIXTEEN DOLLARS ($4,716) same to be 
charged against AIRPORT RECEIPTS RESERVED and credited to the following 
Personal Services accounts: 
 
  LABOR -     $3,843 
OVERTIME -        $615 
BUYBACKS -       $258 
 (Be Adopted) 
 
154-26. ORDER THAT: there be and hereby is appropriated the sum of SEVEN 
HUNDRED FIFTY THOUSAND DOLLARS ($750,000) same to be credited to the 
Fitchburg Public Library renovation and reconstruction project. 
there be and hereby is appropriated the sum of ONE MILLION EIGHT HUNDRED 
EIGHTY THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED SEVENTEEN DOLLARS ($1,880,117) 
from available funds, same to be credited to the Fitchburg Public Library renovation 
and reconstruction project. 
(Be Adopted as amended) 
 
Report read and accepted. Orders adopted by unanimous consent 11/0. 11 members present. Board 
consists of 11 members. 
 
Orders signed by the Mayor October 8, 2026 
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Legislative Affairs Committee 
Meeting of October 6, 2026 
Oral Report 
 
159-26. Paula Caron, Chair, Fitchburg Planning Board: Request to amend Chapter 181 of 
the Fitchburg Zoning Code to establish a temporary zoning moratorium on Locally 
Regulated Commercial Battery Energy Storage Systems (LRC-BESS). 
 
160-26. Paula Caron, Chair, Fitchburg Planning Board, request to amend Chapter 181 of the 
Fitchburg Zoning Code to add a temporary zoning moratorium on large-scale data 
centers. 
 
Report read and accepted. Petitions are being referred to the Planning Board for a Public Hearing  
by unanimous consent 11/0. 11 members present. Board consists of 11 members. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
Public Works Committee 
Meeting of September 29, 2026 
Oral Report 
      
151-26.  Vice President Cruz, on behalf of the residents of Greenhurst Ave. to petition for 
temporary repairs of a private way as outlined in the enclosed petition. 
 (Be Held)  
 
161-26.  City Councilor Bernie Schultz, on behalf of Wayne Shaw of 508 Milk Street, to install 
a berm to stop water runoff from damaging the front yard of his home.  
 (Be Granted) 
 
062-26.  Councilor Fleming on behalf of the residents living at 77 Congress St to install a berm 
in front of the house and around the corner heading toward Lunenburg St.  
 (Be Granted as Amended) 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
VII. ORDERS – FINANCE 
     
Orders stand referred to Finance: 
 
162-26. ORDER THAT: the City of Fitchburg hereby approves the expenditure of grant 
funds from the United Way of North Central Massachusetts, in the approximate 
amount of TWENTY THOUSAND DOLLARS ($20,000), awarded to the city 
Recreation Program from the DESE After School and Out of School Time Program 
Grant to cover the cost of weekly STEAM (Science Technology Engineering Arts 
Math) activities throughout the school year in collaboration with the Fitchburg 
Public Library. 
 
163-26. ORDER THAT: the City of Fitchburg hereby approves the expenditure of a 
donation from the Friends of Coggshall Park, in the approximate amount of 
FIFTEEN THOUSAND DOLLARS $15,000, toward the purchase and installation 
of a new playground at Coggshall Park.
164-26. ORDER THAT: the City of Fitchburg hereby approves an expenditure by the Parks 
Department of FIFTEEN THOUSAND DOLLARS ($15,000) from the  
Henry F. Coggshall Trust toward the purchase and installation of a new playground 
at Coggshall Park. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
VIII. ORDER – OTHER 
 
Motion and second for suspension of rules by unanimous consent 11/0. 11 members present. Board  
Consists of 11 members. 
 
165-26. ORDER THAT: Authorizing the City Clerk to notify the voters of the State 
Election on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. 
 State Election Warrant 2026 
 State Election Warrant 2026 Spanish 
 
Motion and second to adopt Order by unanimous consent 11/0. 11 members present. Board  
Consists of 11 members. 
 
Order signed by the Mayor October 8, 2026. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
IX. ORDINANCES 
 
166-26. AN ORDINANCE: President Zarrella and Vice President Cruz, to amend §3-19 and 
§3-43 of the City Code, concerning the management and responsibilities of the City 
Clerk, as detailed in the enclosed ordinance. 
 Amend §3-19 and §3-43 of the City Code 
 (First Reading) 
 
Motion and second to send Ordinance was sent to a first and second reading and ordered  
advertised by unanimous consent 11/0. 11 members present. Board consists of 11 members. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
167-26.         AN ORDINANCE: That the General Ordinance of the City of Fitchburg, Chapter 164, 
shall be repealed in its entirety. 
 Ref. petition 150-26 
 (First Reading) 
 
Motion and second to send Ordinance was sent to a first and second reading and ordered  
advertised by unanimous consent 11/0. 11 members present. Board consists of 11 members. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
144-26 A.        AN ORDINANCE: Amending Part II General Legislation, Chapter 169, § 59 of the 
Code of the City of Fitchburg as outlined in the enclosed Ordinance. 
                        Amending Chapter 169 § 59    
(Final Reading) 
 
Motion and second to pass Ordinance to a third and final reading, and adopt to be enrolled and 
ordained by unanimous consent 11/0. 11 members present. Board consists of 11 members.  
 
Ordinance signed by the Mayor October 8, 2026.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
144-26 B.        AN ORDINANCE: Amending Part II General Legislation, Chapter 169, § 76 of the 
Code of the City of Fitchburg as outlined in the enclosed Ordinance. 
                        Amending Chapter 169 § 76  
(Final Reading) 
 
Motion and second to pass Ordinance to a third and final reading, and adopt to be enrolled and 
ordained by unanimous consent 11/0. 11 members present. Board consists of 11 members.  
 
Ordinance signed by the Mayor October 8, 2026. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
144-26 C. AN ORDINANCE: Amending Part II General Legislation, Chapter 169, §77 of the 
Code of the City of Fitchburg as outlined in the enclosed Ordinance. 
 Amending Chapter 169  §77 
(Final Reading) 
 
Motion and second to pass Ordinance to a third and final reading, and adopt to be enrolled and 
ordained by unanimous consent 11/0. 11 members present. Board consists of 11 members.  
 
Ordinance signed by the Mayor October 8, 2026. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
155-26. AN ORDINANCE:  by the City Council of the City of Fitchburg that Code of the 
City of Fitchburg, Chapter 169, § 24 titled Vehicles and Traffic is hereby amended 
as follows:  
 
 That the General Ordinances of the City of Fitchburg, Chapter 169, § 24, as most 
recently amended, be further amended by adding the following location to the list of 
streets, or parts thereof, where parking is prohibited: 
  
 NAME OF STREET  SIDE   LOCATION 
 Birch Street Passway  North   From 36 Birch Street 
        Passway to 89 Birch Street 
        Passway. 
 (Ref. petition 054-26) 
(Final Reading) 
 
Motion and second to pass Ordinance to a third and final reading, and adopt to be enrolled and 
ordained by unanimous consent 11/0. 11 members present. Board consists of 11 members.  
 
Ordinance signed by the Mayor October 8, 2026. 
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
X. PETITIONS 
 
Petition stands referred to Legislative Affairs: 
 
168-26. President Zarrella, on behalf of Marisa R. Fleming, to petition for Special 
Legislation relative to the creditable service of Marisa R. Fleming, as outlined in the 
enclosed petition. 
 Special Legislation Relative to Creditable Service 
 (Legislative Affairs) 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
Petitions stand referred to a Public Hearing: 
 
169-26. 7 BEEKMAN ST – Unitil petitions to relocate Pole #8 (Salem St.). The proposed 
Pole #8 would be relocated approximately 26 feet from its original location and 
would be situated approximately 80 feet from Beekman St. and approximately 415 
feet from Spruce St., Fitchburg. 
 (Refer Public Hearing October 20, 2026) 
 
170-26. 470 ALPINE ROAD – Unitil petitions to install a new midspan Pole #30A on 
Alpine Road. The proposed Pole #30A would be situated approximately 52 feet 
from existing Pole #30 and approximately 997 feet from the intersection of 
McIntire Road, Fitchburg. 
 (Refer Public Hearing October 20, 2026) 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
Petition stands referred to the Public Safety Committee: 
 
171-26. Councilor Bowen, on behalf of the Crocker Field Restoration Committee, requests 
that the City investigate and implement enforceable parking controls along Broad 
Street and Circle Street adjacent to Crocker Field to improve parking availability 
during Crocker Field events, particularly in light of ongoing long-term occupancy 
of public on-street parking spaces. 
 (Public Safety) 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
 
 
 
XI. OTHER BUSINESS 
 
 
Next Regular City Council Meeting 
Tuesday, October 20, 2026 7:00 PM 
 
 
The meeting adjourned at 7:44 P.M. 
 
 
___________________________________       
Joanna Bilotta-Simeone, City Clerk
